description:
About the company
 Our client is a fast-growing software company.
 The role
 Raydar is recruiting for this role on behalf of our client. Build and test motion control software that runs on physical robot arms, moving from planning and simulation to live hardware. The work centers on making robots reliable in busy, changing environments, with close contact with the people who use the systems.
 What you'll do
 - Develop algorithms that plan and smooth arm movements through crowded, shifting workspaces.
 - Validate and troubleshoot control code in both simulated and hardware settings, delivering working releases for live machines.
 - Apply computer vision so robots can handle standard tools and equipment built for people.
 - Work directly with partner scientists at external sites to understand needs, propose solutions and support deployment.
 - Look for ways to simplify the software and make the platform more scalable and robust.
 Requirements 
 What we're looking for
 - 2 to 5 years of experience in robotics or related software engineering.
 - Track record of getting software running on live robotic machines.
 - Degree in robotics, electrical engineering, computer science, computer engineering or mechanical engineering from a top school.
 - Professional proficiency in Python.
 - Practical understanding of how articulated machines are planned, guided and controlled.
 Bonus points
 - Hands-on background with precise, fine-grained arm handling or exacting production tasks.
 - Background in lab automation or manufacturing robotics.
 - Familiarity with robotics simulation tools.
 Benefits 
 Compensation and benefits
 - Base salary: USD 148,000 to 230,000 per year
 - Equity
 - Medical and dental coverage
 - Retirement plan
 - Flexible time off
 Location and work model
 - San Francisco, CA, United States
 - On-site, 5 days in-office
 - Full-time
